newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures rallied to reach a new contract high for the third consecutive day on Friday before a wave of profit-taking ahead of the weekend sent the contract back close to Thursday's closing level.

Nevertheless, traders said the market remained well supported and a test of the new contract high at 125.14 next week was still on the cards although it would encounter resistance at 125.20 and 125.40.
The contract reached the high for the day after U.S. bonds got a brief lift from a slight downward revision to second quarter gross domestic product to 4.7 percent.
However, analysts said when the euphoria which had pervaded bond markets earlier in the day faded somewhat, notably in Spain and Italy, French bonds followed suit.
The contract settled at 124.84, up six centimes on the day and up 64 centimes during the week.
The 10-year yield spread over Bunds, using the 6.0 percent 2006 OAT, ended little changed at three basis points on Friday after briefly reaching parity during the early morning rally.
One trader said the ongoing impression that domestic investors had money to invest remained a supportive factor along with the weak French August unemployment figures.
He pointed out that the open interest in the December contract had remained generally static this week, which suggested some investors were probably still waiting on the sidelines.
The French unemployment rate rose to a record 12.6 percent in August. Economists said it underlined the weakness of the French economy and the need for lower interest rates.

December PIBOR also reached a new contract high of 96.32, up three basis points on Friday and six basis points during the week. Notably, the spread over December Euromarks narrowed to 52 basis points, the lowest it has been this year.
The franc ended the European session little changed at 3.3812 per mark, virtually the same level it's finished at for the past three days.
